17: This city… I can't wait to get out.
18: Anywhere without the Shadow Lord's mark would do.
19: Oh no… Grey Guards… I'd better not let them see me.
20: Hey! What are you doing out at this hour?
22: (That was close… I can't get caught by the Guards.)
23: (I promised to be home by evening…) (Mother must be worried…)
27: Then let's rough up his old man.
28: No, leave him. That blacksmith's good. We can get fine swords from him cheap.
31: Ha ha ha, that's a good one! I can just see the blacksmith's sour face!
41: Honestly… You were told to be home by evening. Where would you be without me?
43: But, but, but, but! You're pathetic.
44: Pathetic!? You're the same! You just live off us!
45: True, Jarred and Anna look after me. Which makes me the same as you.
47: This is bad. The Grey Guards know I live here.
50: You want to leave the city, don't you? Go in and talk to Jarred. Everything's ready for your journey.
52: Father… Sorry I'm late. But please, no more reading The Belt of Deltora. I've read it so many times I know it by heart.
55: (I shouldn't have said that. This'll be a long lecture…)
57: (I-I can't breathe. I have to say something…)
58: Barda said a strange thing. That I'm going on a journey.
59: Yes, that's true. And a very dangerous one.
61: Hear me out, then decide for yourself.
63: This… is the Belt of Deltora.
64: What!? The Belt of the royal family? Why is it in our house!?
65: I lived in the palace long ago.
67: And I was the best friend of Endon, last king of Deltora.
69: Yes… He was a naive fool. Who knows where he is or what he's doing now…
71: Who can say. But his child, the royal heir, must be alive. I want you to find that heir. To save this land from the Shadow Lord.
73: Even with an heir, what could anyone do… That's foolish King Endon's child, isn't it?
74: With this Belt, all will be well. First, set the 7 gems in the Belt. When the royal heir wears it…
75: I see, that story you told me once.
76:
Adin persuaded the seven tribes
and gathered the gems.

He set them in a belt he forged
and fastened it around his waist.

The Belt blazed as bright as the sun.
77:
In its light, the seven tribes of
Deltora united and fought.

And so the Shadow Lord was driven away.
78: Yes. The Belt's power should save Deltora, as it did long ago.
79: But Father, this Belt has no gems…
80: …I have to find the gems too?
82: Lief, you may refuse. No one will force you to go. You're still only 16.
85: This is a gift from me. A sword I made. The finest work I've ever done.
88: I made it with many memories, and with love.
91: Don't worry. I can help save this land. I'm glad to go!
92: I meant to go myself, but…
93: Your leg is bad, Father. I understand, don't worry.
96: Lief, aren't you going to tell them? The Grey Guards are after you.
100: Jarred, this puts you in danger too.
101: Don't worry about me. I'll say I threw my son out of the house.
103: Lief, you are not running away from this city. You are setting out to save the world from the Shadow Lord.
107: What a feeble answer. Is it too soon to send you?
114: I'm coming too. I promised Jarred.
118: I'm Barda, former guard of the palace at Del. Pleased to meet you.
120: Not just any guard. A special guard, sworn to protect the king.
124: The Shadow Lord hid the gems of the Belt. Seven gems in seven places.
125: From what Jarred and I found out… one gem is in the Forests of Silence.
127: Terrible monsters live there. That's why even the Grey Guards keep away.
130: Of course not! I just thought no Guards means we're safe.
